title: Far Away from Orbital Space
description: Scoring systems, puzzle design and playtest iteration on a co-op communication puzzler at Luski Game Studio.

items.label: Analog prototypes
items.body: Led analog prototyping to validate the core idea in Miro before anything was built in Unreal.

items.label: Gameplay systems
items.body: Engineered the scoring algorithms, puzzle gating, difficulty scaling and meta-progression loops, keeping the cooperative mechanics in systemic sync.

items.label: Puzzle design
items.body: Co-designed the puzzles with the game and level design teams, around player communication.

items.label: Playtest iteration
items.body: Ran closed and open playtests, including live events, and iterated on what came back.

blocks.html: The target was a high-synergy cooperative loop built on asymmetrical communication. To keep cognitive load from turning chaotic while holding a challenging cadence, I mapped and validated every systemic interaction on paper and in Miro before engineering touched it.

items.label: The problem
items.body: Early playtest cohorts hit opaque scoring feedback. Players could not connect their in-game actions to their final performance, which read as mechanical friction.

items.label: The iteration
items.body: I built an analytical feedback spreadsheet to rebalance the scoring variables and weights, restructuring the algorithm so secondary objectives became high-reward modifiers tied to remaining level time.

items.label: The result
items.body: Teams recognised their compounding multipliers immediately, and remaining match time turned into bonus economy points per dish served.

blocks.title: Score as time remaining grows — placeholder curve, swap for the real weights

blocks.text: Puzzles you have to talk through

blocks.html: Rather than mechanical locks, the puzzle framework was built on communication friction. Each puzzle stress-tests a different faculty — short-term memory, semantic interpretation, physical synchronisation — turning human cognitive limits into cooperative hooks.

items.label: The mental layer
items.body: Visually dense, high-similarity glyphs that require a careful verbal breakdown between partners to avoid execution errors.

items.label: The memory layer
items.body: Asymmetrical data relays needing rapid short-term recall and sequential message passing, under time pressure, before the information resets.

items.label: The physical layer
items.body: Mechanically isolated layout interactions demanding precise, verbally synchronised execution, balancing movement against data delivery.

blocks.html: Every puzzle idea was evaluated against all three layers before it went in.
Happy to walk through the documentation, behaviour trees and tuning decisions behind this project.
